evidence: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:47-58 handleAdd sets isInvalidEmail=true on failure but never resets it to false on a successful parse; MultiEmail setValue (line 72) is plain setMultiEmailValue with no reset. Only the Cancel button (lines 89-92) clears it. Even a successful add doesn't clear it (onSuccess lines 35-40 omit it), and closing via onOpenChange (line 60) doesn't either, so the banner stays after the user fixes the input and can still be there when the dialog is reopened.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-550 sendAddGuestsEmails takes no eventTypeMetadata and never calls eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail (defined at lines 81-87). Every sibling sender does check them (e.g. sendLocationChangeEmails lines 503/515, sendRescheduledEmails 194/206). addGuests.handler.ts:168 doesn't pass booking.eventType.metadata. So host and attendee emails go out even when the event type has disableStandardEmails set.

addGuests.handler.ts:127 sets evt.description = booking.description. booking.description is the booker's additionalNotes (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/createBooking.ts:212). BaseScheduledEmail.tsx:87 renders calEvent.description. evt never sets hideCalendarNotes (lines 124-147), and sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:541-545) sends AttendeeScheduledEmail/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail without the hideCalendarNotes stripping that sendScheduledEmails does (email-manager.ts:119). So notes that are meant to be hidden reach the new guests, just through description rather than additionalNotes.

addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270 shows isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER, and isTeamOwner (286-295) matches OWNER only, so the && reduces to 'is owner'. Team ADMINs are wrongly blocked (the real bug), but owners are not, so the claim overstates it. The fix is to use || or just isTeamAdmin.

addGuests.handler.ts:70-72 lowercases the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries, but lines 74-78 compare the raw guest string (not lowercased) with blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) and guest === attendee.email. 'Bad@X.com' gets past a blacklist entry 'bad@x.com', and an existing attendee can be added again with different casing. addGuests.schema.ts z.string().email() doesn't normalize case.

The server schema addGuests.schema.ts:3-6 has no uniqueness check, and the handler filter at addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 only removes existing attendees and blacklisted emails, not duplicates within the input. createMany (lines 100-104) would insert duplicate attendee rows. Only the client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:25-28 dedupes, and a direct tRPC call skips it.

addGuests.handler.ts:168 calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the raw input instead of uniqueGuests (line 74). In email-manager.ts:541-545 newGuests.includes(attendee.email) decides who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail. If the input mixes new emails with an already-existing attendee, that existing attendee gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the add-guests notification. Low impact but a real bug.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:14 reassigns value = value || []. This is harmless (a local rebinding, no mutation of the caller's array), and value is typed string[] (non-optional) so it's only a defensive default. A default in destructuring would be cleaner, but there's no functional impact.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:26 uses key={index}, and removal from the middle is supported (onClickAddon splice, lines 39-43). The EmailField inputs are fully controlled (value={field}, line 29), so the displayed values stay correct after removal. Only transient DOM state (focus, tooltip) may attach to the wrong row. Using the email as the key isn't safe either, since duplicates and empty strings are allowed. The practical impact is minor.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:19-75 uses a ternary with a <></> else-branch (line 74); `value.length > 0 && (...)` would be equivalent. This is purely cosmetic. Note that `value.length && ...` without a comparison would render 0, so the ternary isn't wrong.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:25-28 builds the uniqueness check with new Set(emails), which is case-sensitive, so User@x.com and user@x.com pass. The server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) has no uniqueness check at all, so the authoritative fix belongs server-side (see ids 4/5). Lowercasing in the client refine is a cheap UX improvement.
